name: Greymarrow Detach-Panel Night Ops Set
description: Everything about this set is designed to change. The primary jacket is a hip-length blouson in matte grey-brown — the color of unpainted ferrocrete, utterly unremarkable — with four snap-off exterior panels: two chest, two shoulder. Each panel swaps out independently, and a runner carrying a small pouch of alternates can change the jacket's visible silhouette and color blocking in under ninety seconds. The base jacket beneath the panels is plain enough to wear alone. Inside, a double-wall front panel conceals a rigid holster frame that can be reconfigured for two compacts, one full-frame, or a row of tool loops. The back yoke has a full spinal channel — a wide open-seam corridor running from collar to hem that accommodates external spinal rig hardware, closing around it with a series of silent magnetic tabs. Gene-compatible rear venting panels accommodate non-functional wings or large dorsal geneware modifications with snap-bar expansion. Paired trousers are in near-black slate with a maroon pinstripe too subtle to read at distance — Tier 2 enough to vanish in a crowd, Tier 3 enough to enter a building lobby. Thigh zip pockets are scanner-lined to mask small metal objects from passive detection. Footwear is a flat-soled runner's shoe in dark graphite synthetic mesh over a hard composite plate, lace-free with a single diagonal strap closure. A thin balaclava in matching grey-brown microfibre is folded in the inside collar pocket — full face cover in two seconds, gone in three.
functionality: Interchangeable snap-off exterior panels for rapid silhouette change; reconfigurable internal holster frame; magnetic-tab spinal rig channel (full back accommodation); gene-compatible dorsal expansion panels for wing or large geneware; scanner-lined thigh pockets; Tier 2-3 crowd-compatible trouser aesthetic; stored balaclava in collar pocket; lace-free fast footwear
what_it_says: This is a professional who learned from a job that went wrong because they were too recognizable. Everything about this set is designed to be different five minutes later. The maroon pinstripe in the trousers is the only vanity — a runner's private joke that they're still themselves underneath all the adaptations.
worn_by: operatives who work the same area repeatedly and need to vary their appearance
manufacturer: Greymarrow Fab — unlicensed, Shelf-adjacent workshop, known for modular construction
story_hooks: A runner's panel pouch is lost during an early chase, leaving them locked into one visible configuration for the rest of a multi-stage job where they need to appear as two different people.
The scanner-lined thigh pockets are old stock — a newer passive scanner at the checkpoint reads right through them, flagging the ceramic blade inside.
A spinal rig user's magnetic tabs start responding to an electromagnetic pulse deployed by security, causing the back channel to seal shut around the hardware mid-movement.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately unremarkable modular combat outfit. The matte grey-brown jacket reads as utilitarian and forgettable at first glance, but its four independently swappable snap-panels hint at tactical flexibility. The silhouette is athletic and compact—hip-length blouson that doesn't advertise its function. Paired with near-black slate trousers bearing a maroon pinstripe barely visible at distance. The overall impression is 'someone who needs to move without being remembered.'
physical_description.fit: Slim but not tight—built for unrestricted movement and layering of gear beneath. The jacket sits close to the torso but with enough room for concealed hardware and spinal rig accommodation. Trousers are straight-legged with a low, secure waistband. Footwear is minimal and ground-responsive, designed for sprint work.
physical_description.primary_material: Jacket outer: proprietary synth-wool blend in matte finish, designed to dampen visual and thermal signature. Interior panels: ballistic-weave composite. Trousers: treated nanofibre cotton blend. Footwear: graphite synthetic mesh bonded to hard composite plate. Balaclava: microfibre thermal-neutral microknit.
physical_description.texture: The jacket exterior has a flat, almost chalky matte finish—no sheen to catch light. Snap-off panels have subtle raised edges for tactile removal in darkness. Interior reveals tightly woven ballistic texture, almost felt-like. Trousers fabric is smooth but gripping. Shoe sole is hard and unforgiving. Balaclava is soft, frictionless microfibre.
physical_description.color_scheme: Base jacket and balaclava: weathered grey-brown (ferrocrete grey). Trousers: near-black slate with maroon pinstripe thin enough to disappear at 10 meters. Footwear: dark graphite. The interchangeable snap panels suggest potential for color-blocking—neutral palette dominates, with tactical accent possibilities.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: silent magnetic tabs along spinal channel for rear venting; snap-bar expansion frames for dorsal geneware; four heavy-duty snaps securing each exterior panel. Trousers: friction-fit waistband with discrete magnetic closure, dual thigh zips with scanner-lining. Footwear: single diagonal friction strap, no laces. Balaclava: no closure—pull-on.
distinctive_features: Four independently swappable snap-off exterior panels (chest x2, shoulder x2) enabling sub-90-second silhouette/color changes
Double-wall front concealing reconfigurable rigid holster frame (2 compact / 1 full-frame / tool loop layouts)
Full spinal channel along back yoke with silent magnetic tab closure for external rig accommodation
Gene-compatible rear venting panels with snap-bar expansion for non-functional wings or dorsal geneware
Thigh zip pockets with internal scanner-lining for passive metal detection masking
Integrated grey-brown microfibre balaclava stored in inside collar pocket
Lace-free footwear with minimal profile and hard composite plate for silent movement
Deliberately unremarkable factory finish—designed to blend with urban infrastructure
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 hybrid. The modular design and internal hardware frame signal corporate or specialist training. The matte finish and color palette allow Tier 3 entry into corporate lobbies while retaining street-viable anonymity. Price point and manufacturing origin (unlicensed Shelf-adjacent workshop) push it toward accessible mid-tier rather than corpo luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by corporate security contractors, street-tier fixers, black-ops runners, and anyone who needs to change appearance on a dime without drawing attention. The engineering screams 'military-adjacent'—but the unlicensed Greymarrow origin keeps it deniable. This is the outfit of someone who moves through the GLMZ with purpose and wants no witnesses.
physical_description.condition_typical: New-condition examples are pristine, with crisp snap-panel engagement and unmarked fabric. Field-worn sets show subtle creasing along movement lines, minor scuffs on the shoe composite, and slight fading of the maroon pinstripe. The interior holster frame may show wear marks from hardware. Storage pouches for spare panels often develop small tears. Balaclava may be lint-dusted from collar pocket residence.

image_prompt: Fashion photo of a sleek, unremarkable grey-brown modular night ops jacket on a lean cyberpunk model with visible minimal augmentation (maybe a subtle neck port or biolume fingertips). Model wears the jacket with near-black slate trousers and graphite runners. Four detachable snap panels are visible on chest and shoulders, each panel slightly offset to show the interlock system. The model's hand reaches toward a thigh pocket, scanner-lined interior faintly visible. Dark industrial warehouse backdrop—ferrocrete walls, blue neon edge lighting casting cool shadows. Balaclava is folded visibly in the inside collar pocket. The overall mood is tense, professional, utterly forgettable.
